In mathematics, the '''Saito–Kurokawa lift''' (or '''lifting''') takes [[elliptic modular form]]s to [[Siegel modular form]]s of degree 2. The existence of this lifting was conjectured in 1977 independently by [[Hiroshi Saito (mathematician)|Hiroshi Saito]] and {{harvs|txt|first=Nobushige|last=Kurokawa |authorlink=Nobushige Kurokawa|year=1978}}. Its existence was almost proved by {{harvs|txt|last=Maass|authorlink=Hans Maass|year1=1979a|year2=1979b|year3=1979c}}, and {{harvtxt|Andrianov|1979}} and {{harvtxt|Zagier|1981}} completed the proof.

==Statement==
The Saito–Kurokawa lift ''σ''<sub>''k''</sub> takes level 1 modular forms ''f'' of weight 2''k''&nbsp;−&nbsp;2 to level 1 Siegel modular forms of degree 2 and weight ''k''. The L-functions (when ''f'' is a Hecke eigenforms) are related by ''L''(''s'',''σ''<sub>''k''</sub>(''f''))&nbsp;=&nbsp;ζ(''s''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''k''&nbsp;+&nbsp;2)ζ(''s''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''k''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)''L''(''s'',&nbsp;''f'').

The Saito–Kurokawa lift can be constructed as the composition of the following three mappings:
# The Shimura correspondence from level 1 modular forms of weight 2''k''&nbsp;−&nbsp;2 to a space of level 4 modular forms of weight ''k''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1/2 in the Kohnen plus-space.
#A map from the Kohnen plus-space to the space of [[Jacobi form]]s of index 1 and weight&nbsp;''k'', studied by [[Martin Eichler|Eichler]] and Zagier.
# A map from the space of Jacobi forms of index 1 and weight ''k'' to the Siegel modular forms of degree 2, introduced by Maass.

The Saito–Kurokawa lift can be generalized to forms of higher level.

The image is the '''Spezialschar''' (special band), the space of Siegel modular forms whose Fourier coefficients satisfy
:<math>
a
\begin{pmatrix}
n & t/2 \\
t/2 & m
\end{pmatrix}
=\sum_{d\mid t,m,n} d^{k-1}a
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & t/2d \\
t/2d & nm/d^2
\end{pmatrix}.
</math>

==See also==

*[[Doi–Naganuma lifting]], a similar lift to Hilbert modular forms.
*[[Ikeda lift]], a generalization to Siegel modular forms of higher degree.
